prompt: Which link of the iOS chain names the app, by its bundle identifier?

choices.text: The certificate
choices.why: The certificate says who signs, not which app.

choices.text: The device list of the profile
choices.why: That says where a build may run.

choices.text: The App ID
choices.why: Right. Bundle identifier plus capabilities.

choices.text: Apple's intermediate certificate
choices.why: That is the top of the chain, the same for everybody.

prompt: A new developer downloads the team's distribution certificate from the portal onto their Mac, and Xcode still cannot sign. What is missing?

choices.text: The private key, left on the Mac that made it
choices.why: Right. The portal holds only the certificate, the public half.

choices.text: A provisioning profile for each tester's device
choices.why: An App Store build has no device list.

choices.text: A second Apple account
choices.why: One team, one account; she needs the key, not an account.

choices.text: A newer version of Xcode
choices.why: No version of Xcode can sign without the private key.

prompt: Push notifications are switched on in the planner's App ID but missing from the app's entitlements. What is the likely symptom?

choices.text: Apple rejects the whole developer account at the next review
choices.why: Accounts are not judged on entitlements.

choices.text: The app crashes on every launch, before any screen appears
choices.why: Missing entitlements do not crash an app at launch.

choices.text: Notifications arrive twice
choices.why: Nothing duplicates them; they fail or work.

choices.text: A signing error, or push that silently never arrives
choices.why: Right. The two lists disagree, and the signature is built from the entitlements.

prompt: Match each link to what it says.

pairs.right: what the app may do, baked into the signature
the tie between them, and where it may run

right_distractors: the price of the app in each country

prompt: The planner's distribution certificate expired last night. The membership is current. What happens to the people who installed it from the App Store?

choices.text: The app stops opening until they update
choices.why: That is what an expired ad hoc profile does, not a store app.

choices.text: Nothing; the team just cannot upload new builds
choices.why: Right. Apple's documentation says store apps are not affected.

choices.text: The app is removed from their phones
choices.why: Nothing removes an installed app for this.

choices.text: Apple re-signs it with a fresh certificate automatically
choices.why: Apple re-signs at distribution; your certificate is yours to renew.

prompt: How many iPhones can a team register for ad hoc builds in one membership year?
In March, the team has registered 100 iPhones and removes 30 old ones. A new tester's iPhone arrives in April. What can the team do?

choices.text: Register it in one of the 30 freed slots
choices.why: Removing a device does not free its slot until the next membership year.

choices.text: Invite her through TestFlight
choices.why: Right. That is much of why TestFlight exists.

choices.text: Buy another 100 slots
choices.why: Apple sells no extra slots.

choices.text: Send her the development build
choices.why: A development build has the same device list problem.

prompt: Which builds stop opening on a tester's phone when their profile expires? Choose every one.

choices.text: A development build
choices.why: Right. Its profile has a date.

choices.text: An ad hoc build
choices.why: Right. Same: the profile governs it.

choices.text: An App Store build
choices.why: Apple re-signed it; your profile's date no longer matters to it.

choices.text: An Android APK signed by the upload key
choices.why: Android signatures carry no profile.

prompt: Why does Xcode's automatic signing stop being enough the day a team adds a build server?

choices.text: Automatic signing is forbidden for App Store builds
choices.why: It is allowed; one developer can ship that way.

choices.text: It creates a new App ID on every build
choices.why: The App ID is registered once.

choices.text: Build servers cannot run Xcode
choices.why: A Mac build server runs Xcode fine.

choices.text: The server has nobody to click Fix Issue and none of the keys
choices.why: Right. The credentials live in people's keychains.

prompt: Match each answer to who holds the iOS signing credentials.

pairs.right: the keychain of the Mac that made them
an encrypted repository every machine reads

prompt: A React Native team has no Mac and must ship the iOS build next week. Which path from the lesson fits?

choices.text: EAS Build
choices.why: Right. It holds the credentials and builds on its own Macs.

choices.text: Sign on Linux with the distribution certificate
choices.why: The iOS build and its signing need Xcode, which runs only on macOS.

choices.text: fastlane match on a Linux runner
choices.why: match shares the credentials, but signing and building still need a Mac.

choices.text: An ad hoc build from Android Studio
choices.why: Android Studio builds Android.

prompt: Why does `expiry.ts` set `process.exitCode` to 1 when a certificate needs attention?

choices.text: Node requires it after reading a certificate
choices.why: Node exits 0 by default whatever was read.

choices.text: To delete the expired file
choices.why: An exit status deletes nothing.

choices.text: So a pipeline step fails and somebody sees it
choices.why: Right. A nightly job goes red a month early.

choices.text: To make the output shorter
choices.why: The output is the same; only the status changes.

prompt: On a Mac, `security cms -D -i profile.mobileprovision` prints a profile as text, and its date is the key named ___.
Which of these has no expiry date at all?

choices.text: The .p8 key for the App Store Connect API
choices.why: Right. It is revoked, never renewed.

choices.text: The development profile
choices.why: Its date is ExpirationDate.

choices.text: The developer program membership itself, once paid
choices.why: It lapses a year after enrolment.

choices.text: The Apple Distribution certificate
choices.why: It has one, and the script reads it.

prompt: `expiry.ts` printed `RENEW 20 days` for the distribution certificate. What should the team do this week?

choices.text: Revoke it at once
choices.why: Revoking can mark uploaded builds Invalid Binary, for no gain.

choices.text: Nothing until it expires, since store apps keep working
choices.why: They keep working, but the team cannot ship until it renews.

choices.text: Renew it now, and check the release build still signs
choices.why: Right. Renewing early is cheap; renewing on launch day is not, and the shared set has to carry the new one.

choices.text: Remove the app from sale
choices.why: Nothing about an expiry requires it.

prompt: Put the links of the iOS chain in the order they are created for a new app.
items: a private key and a certificate signing request on the Mac
the App ID with its capabilities
the provisioning profile that ties them
the build, signed and with the profile embedded

prompt: An enterprise company's in-house app, a lapsed Apple Developer program, and an App Store app all depend on dates. Which one keeps working for people who already installed it?

choices.text: The in-house app, once its profile expires
choices.why: An expired in-house profile stops the app from launching.

choices.text: The App Store app, after the membership lapses
choices.why: Right. It leaves the store, and installed copies still run.

choices.text: None of them
choices.why: One of them does, by Apple's own documentation.

choices.text: An ad hoc build, after its profile expires
choices.why: Ad hoc builds stop opening with the profile.

prompt: Which Android piece plays the role of the iOS App ID?

choices.text: The upload key registered with Google Play
choices.why: That is a credential, not the app's name.

choices.text: The versionCode written in the build file
choices.why: That changes with every release.

choices.text: The debug keystore
choices.why: That signs debug builds on one computer.

choices.text: The package name in the manifest
choices.why: Right. Both name the app and cannot change once published.
